mbm-1576.clue: I take my glasses off to read this map.
mbm-1576.quote: Under the canopy the railway curved round a red barn just like the loop on my brother's train set. I drew both from memory when I got home. His barn needs moving an inch.

mbm-1577.clue: I bring a sponge for a very fussy passenger.
mbm-1577.quote: My cousin's toy stegosaurus rides in the bow of our canoe. One rainy afternoon we bailed his little hollow back before we bailed the boat. My cousin remembers exactly who got rescued first.

mbm-1578.clue: My slippers tell you who did it.
mbm-1578.quote: When the mystery goes to commercial we point our slippers at the suspect's picture in the paper. Last Friday mine pointed at the radiator until the last minute. I stand by my method.

mbm-1579.clue: The secret is in the oven mitt.
mbm-1579.quote: My great-aunt left one striped oven mitt and no fabric big enough to match. I unpicked its cuff for the red border of a soup-bowl quilt. Every square reminds us of something she cooked.

mbm-1580.clue: We save our receipts from imaginary hotels.
mbm-1580.quote: Dad cut hotel doors out of a cereal box for our board game. When you check out, he slips the bill under the tiny door. I still owe him two green beads for room service.

mbm-1581.clue: I've got four seasons on the back of my chair.
mbm-1581.quote: I'm quilting the same pear tree four times, one for each season. Last night I stitched a crow into the bare branches. Now my niece insists it's the same crow hiding in all the other blocks.

mbm-1582.clue: The last frame is always for the feet.
mbm-1582.quote: I took a beautiful formal picture of the choir. Then I tilted my camera down. Twenty black robes, nineteen pairs of dress shoes and one small pair of green flippers under the shortest robe.

mbm-1583.clue: I'm waiting for the chair to change color again.
mbm-1583.quote: I paint a tiny portrait of our barber's front chair whenever he reupholsters it. We lined them up in the window. One customer recognized the exact green in which he got his first haircut.

mbm-1584.clue: My needlework has a secret gardener.
mbm-1584.quote: I embroidered my first flower on my aunt's pollera. She gave my crooked stem a second leaf and said now it was growing toward the sun. I know my flower by that leaf when she dances.

mbm-1585.clue: I make my best knots on the bus.
mbm-1585.quote: I crocheted a blue cover for the worn handle of Mum's shopping bag. We took it to market and a seller asked if I'd do his basket. I came home with two skeins and six peaches.

mbm-1586.clue: The remote comes with its own pillow.
mbm-1586.quote: Our sofa has one spring that squeaks through the quiet bits of the show. I sewed a little pillow for the remote and tucked it over the spring. The detective finally got to whisper his last line.

mbm-1587.clue: I like the seats under the broken star.
mbm-1587.quote: The ceiling of our old cinema has a painted night sky. One star chipped off above my favorite row. I know where to sit by finding the spot where the Little Dipper leaks.

mbm-1588.clue: Don't cut that last bit of red thread.
mbm-1588.quote: My father gave me his coat to mend. I sewed a red stitch on the inside of each cuff so he can tell which end is the front in a dark hallway. Now he'll only wear red on the inside.

mbm-1589.clue: I name my characters after lost umbrellas.
mbm-1589.quote: I work on my book in the café beside a bin of forgotten umbrellas. The stern detective got the brass handle. The nervous witness got the one that keeps opening by itself.

mbm-1590.clue: Our smallest dumbbell sings a B-flat.
mbm-1590.quote: The brass chime tied to my gym bag rings when I set the weights down too hard. My training partner can tell from across the room whether to applaud or play conductor.

mbm-1591.clue: There's a compass in my sandwich tin.
mbm-1591.quote: Fog rolled across the pond during our dawn paddle. My friend held the little compass above the sandwiches. The mist lifted halfway back and we found our picnic spot by the smell of toast.

mbm-1592.clue: I take my time tying the towel afterward.
mbm-1592.quote: At the outdoor onsen I watched a tuft of snow sag lower and lower on one pine branch. Everyone in the bath went quiet till it fell. Such applause for such a little plop.

mbm-1593.clue: I keep the rope handle on the mantel all winter.
mbm-1593.quote: My sister painted two red arrows on my water-ski handle where my hands belong. Now our cat sits between them in January. I think she's training for the summer.

mbm-1594.clue: I made a rule about laundry baskets.
mbm-1594.quote: The best catch I ever made landed in the clean laundry behind me. After that we played disc golf with three empty baskets. Nobody was allowed to bring socks.

mbm-1595.clue: One quilt square is supposed to be upside down.
mbm-1595.quote: I made a blanket out of patterns from Grandad's old ties. He always wore the duck tie crooked, so I turned that square on its side. The duck looks perfectly at home.

mbm-1596.clue: My trail snack knows where we're going.
mbm-1596.quote: Before we leave, my niece cuts a mountain into the paper around each sandwich. We ate beside a ridge that matched the last one, and she held lunch up like a map.

mbm-1597.clue: I carry chalk for my boots.
mbm-1597.quote: At each rest stop my hiking buddy and I compare tread prints on the flat rocks. His heel has a chipped star. When we got separated I followed those funny stars right to the spring.

mbm-1598.clue: We keep the orange peel for the scoreboard.
mbm-1598.quote: The wind took our pencil during beach volleyball. We kept score by tearing strips off an orange peel and hanging them on the net post. At match point the gulls got very interested.

mbm-1599.clue: There's a nickel stitched inside my dance shoe.
mbm-1599.quote: My first dance teacher lent me bus fare after a class ran late. Years later I sewed a little pocket inside my shoe for a nickel. I take it out when a new dancer needs a ride.

mbm-1600.clue: Grandma has a favorite cup for this one.
mbm-1600.quote: I hide a sugar cube under one teacup and slide it between the others. Grandma follows every move with her finger. At the reveal she drops it into her tea and declares the magician dismissed.
